title: HeteroFL-LoRA: Federated LoRA Fine-Tuning Across Heterogeneous LFMs via Singular Value Collaboration

problem.claim: Federated LoRA updates cannot be directly aggregated effectively when clients use heterogeneous base LFMs because the updates are anchored to model-specific pre-trained weights.

gap.claim: Existing federated LoRA studies assume that all clients share the same LFM and use identical pre-trained weights.

contributions.claim: HeteroFL-LoRA is a federated framework for LoRA fine-tuning across heterogeneous LFMs.
The framework represents LoRA updates through singular value adjustments to decouple them from model-specific pre-trained weights.
A Singular Matrix–Guided Subspace Projection enables cross-subspace mapping and aggregation of heterogeneous clients' LoRA updates in a unified representation space.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HeteroFL-LoRA achieves effective and robust collaboration across heterogeneous LFMs.
The authors report that the framework maintains advantages in training and communication efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated LoRA supports parameter-efficient, privacy-preserving fine-tuning of LFMs across data silos.
Existing approaches assume identical client LFMs, an assumption that rarely holds in real-world deployments; direct aggregation can degrade collaborative performance with heterogeneous models.
HeteroFL-LoRA uses singular value adjustments and Singular Matrix–Guided Subspace Projection to map and aggregate updates across heterogeneous LFMs.
The authors report effective knowledge transfer and robust collaboration across different LFMs with training and communication efficiency advantages.

source_observation.claim: Model-specific parameter updates may be incompatible for direct aggregation across heterogeneous base models.

interpretation.claim: A shared representation space can be a prerequisite for collaborative optimization across heterogeneous model instances.

application.claim: When distributed participants use different base models, consider transforming updates into a model-agnostic or unified representation before aggregation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy applies beyond the described heterogeneous LFM and LoRA setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the heterogeneous LFMs, datasets, baselines, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or define the reported training and communication efficiency advantages.
